basic_info.chief_complaint: Traumatic fracture of upper front tooth

chief_complaint.chief_complaint: Traumatic fracture of upper front tooth

oral_examination.oral_examination: 11 Crown root fracture, the labial side is 2mm above the gums, the lingual side is 3mm below the gums, and the pulp is exposed. CBCT shows that the root length is acceptable and there is no obvious abnormality in the apex.

treatment_plan.definitive: Plan 1: Root canal treatment and post crown restoration\nOption 2: Pull out and plant immediately\nThe patient chooses option one, informs the cost, related treatment process and risks, and agrees to the treatment.
treatment_plan.notes: Instruct patients to avoid eating foods that are too cold/hot/hard/sticky. If you have looseness and discomfort, you should follow up in time and make an appointment by phone before coming.

source_handle: Under local anesthesia with articaine, one-time root canal treatment, length 15mm, temporarily glued back the fractured crown
